proof.heading: Trusted by

facts.text: Founded Love the Kids Rwanda, a registered non-profit that provides scholarships for children from vulnerable families to attend school in Rwanda.
Selected as a Mandela Washington Fellow through the U.S. Department of State's Young African Leaders Initiative, at Appalachian State University in North Carolina.
Laureate of the French Government's Human Rights Prize in Paris.

site.name: Jean Claude Muhire
site.roles: Lived Experience Advocate · Community Builder · Social Impact Leader

bridge.label: Why marketing, for hospitals, schools and NGOs
bridge.paragraph: Jean Claude began in marketing and branding, which is the work of shaping how an organisation speaks and what it repeatedly does. He now brings that to hospitals, schools and NGOs, where people need to feel they belong before they can give their best.

themes.heading: What your people walk away with

items.title: Lived experience
items.text: Your people hear a real story, and see their own in it.

items.title: Leadership
items.text: Leaders leave with a clearer sense of how they show up when it is hard.

items.title: Belonging
items.text: Teams leave knowing what makes people feel they belong, and what quietly pushes them out.

items.title: Turning stories into action
items.text: The room leaves with one thing to do on Monday.

items.name: NGOs
items.text: For teams who came for the mission and are tired. Purpose, retention, and holding a team together.
items.photoAlt: A team talking together around a table (provisional stock photo)

items.name: Hospitals
items.text: For frontline staff under pressure. Burnout, morale, and remembering why they chose this work.
items.photoAlt: Two healthcare workers in scrubs and masks (provisional stock photo)

items.name: Schools
items.text: For staff and students. Culture, belonging, and a school where everyone has a place.
items.photoAlt: A student reading aloud in a full classroom (provisional stock photo)

note.text: Jean Claude doesn't teach leadership from a textbook. He speaks from what he has lived.
